fix(voice): end a session that a socket drop left open
commits.body:
After a socket drop the connection reads `.disconnected` while
Socket.IO is still retrying. The chat took that for "already over":
leaving the screen, or leaving voice, skipped the teardown. The session
kept the system's input mute and went on listening for the AirPods
stem, so a press on another voice screen could silence that screen
with nothing showing it. The session itself could also come back with
no voice controls on screen.

commits.headline: fix(voice): give the system's input mute one owner at a time
commits.body:
iOS has one input mute for the whole app, and listening for its
changes is what opts the app into the AirPods stem press. A chat used
to listen for as long as its screen was alive, so a stem press on
another voice screen could silence that screen's mic with nothing on
screen saying so.

commits.headline: feat(chat): mark what was written while the chat was off screen

A "New" divider sits above the first message written while the app was
in the background, such as the turns of a voice conversation held with

already streaming when the reader left is not marked, and neither is
one that arrives once they are back. It stays until a message is sent
or the app next goes to the background.

commits.body: A session in the error state is not over: a socket error leaves the socket, which reconnects by itself, and possibly the mic. commits.headline: fix(chat): stop the Latest pill and empty state resizing the timeline
commits.body: The scroll view shared a ZStack with the "Latest" pill and the empty state. A ZStack grows to fit a child that is taller than the space on offer, and takes the scroll view with it. The pill carried the bottom safe-area inset as padding, about 400 pt with the keyboard up in a timeline about 240 pt tall. Once it showed, the scroll view reached behind the composer: the newest reply rested out of sight, the timeline never read as being at the bottom again, and the pill never cleared.

commits.body:
The startup check exited 1 whenever EVERNOTE_CONSUMER_KEY or

commits.headline: docs: make the HTTP launcher work on Linux and with EnvironmentFile
commits.body:
The systemd example invoked a wrapper whose fetch() unconditionally called
macOS's `security`, so on Linux it never read secret-tool values and exited
78 before binding a listener — the unit would restart forever. Uncommenting
EnvironmentFile didn't help either, because the wrapper overwrote those
variables with Keychain lookups.

commits.headline: docs: add HTTP transport deployment and supervision guide
commits.body:
HTTP mode moves process supervision from the MCP client to the operator,
but the docs only covered how to turn it on. Nothing said what keeps the
process running, where its logs belong, or how to pass caller keys without
writing them into a world-readable service file.

commits.headline: fix(mcp-evernote): reject an explicitly empty caller list at install time
commits.body:
install.sh used ${EVHTTPD_CALLERS:-default}, so an explicitly empty list was
replaced by the three default callers and rendered into the plist. The
launcher then received a non-empty list, and its own empty-list guard — which
exists precisely to fail closed here — could never fire. The installer
silently contradicted the behaviour the launcher declares.

commits.headline: feat(mcp-evernote): track the shared Evernote HTTP daemon as a module
commits.body:
Switching Claude Desktop from stdio to remote MCP moved the Evernote server
from "a process each client starts and owns" to "a process something else
must keep running" — and nothing was keeping it running. This adds the
launcher and LaunchAgent that do, so they survive a machine rebuild.

commits.headline: fix(research): run resumes from the committed responses.jsonl.gz
commits.body:
On a fresh clone only responses.jsonl.gz exists (the plain file is gitignored).
run looked only at the plain file, so it re-scheduled all 1,680 cells as paid
LLM calls, and the plain file it then created took precedence in
read_responses, so a partial or interrupted run (including run --only <arm>)
hid the committed rows from score and analyze.

commits.headline: fix(research): analyze handles a Studio arm priced by an explicit ladder
commits.body:
README documents `"ladder"` as an alternative to `"multiple"` for an arm's added
tier, but analyze read `["multiple"]` unconditionally for the price curve, so
such a config raised KeyError after elicitation and embedding had already been
paid for. Read it with .get and compute the arc elasticity only between points
that both have a multiplier.

commits.headline: fix(research): analyze no longer truncates the committed responses.jsonl.gz
commits.body:
With only the committed responses.jsonl.gz present (a fresh clone; the plain
responses.jsonl is gitignored), analyze opened that file for writing before
reading it, so the documented no-API rerun replaced the raw responses with an
empty gzip. Read the rows first. analyze now reproduces every committed output
byte for byte, report.html included.

commits.body:

another seed, model, temperature, prompt text or persona source silently

Codex review (P2, adapter.py classify_text): with no stale-value sidecar the
only way to call classify_text was an empty collection, which made every
answer look stale-free. aggregate then accepted those verdicts as fully

commits.headline: Keep implement-and-merge tasks on the change lane (#2564)
commits.body:
## Why
PR #2491 was dispatched as `mode: implement` with an explicit resolve,
push, and merge. `classifyWorkload` returned `verify` because the task
also contained `node --test` and `test/` paths, and `resolve` / `merge`
/ `push` are not in the change-verb list. `task-delegation.js` then set
the worker to `mode: investigate` because a verify workload is
non-mutating, so the worker stayed read-only and never pushed.

fix(eval): ignore environment proxies in the memprobe transport
commits.body:
build_opener installs a default ProxyHandler that reads http(s)_proxy. With a
proxy configured and no_proxy not covering loopback, requests that
assert_loopback had accepted were routed through that proxy, carrying the
X-Api-Key header and the recall query off loopback. The opener now installs
ProxyHandler({}) so the environment cannot reroute this transport.

commits.headline: fix(eval): refuse HTTP redirects in the memprobe transport
commits.body:
urllib follows redirects without re-running assert_loopback and forwards
the X-Api-Key header, so a loopback endpoint that answered with a redirect
could send the API key to a non-loopback host. AutoMem never redirects, so
the transport now raises ProtocolError on any redirect instead of following.

(arXiv:2606.24595): isolated per-user tags, full-store (by-tag) and top-k
(/recall) access, separate recovery/answer/abstention metrics, and
not_scored reports whenever no judge ran. No upstream code or data is
vendored and no model is called. Tracked in #100.

- A `git init` checkout has files and no commit, so cutting a worktree
dies on `HEAD^{commit}`. Seed one root commit when the repository has no
history at all, and still refuse when some other branch already has
history.

points at a commit. Seeding runs only after that lookup finds nothing.
- A rejected seed puts the original index back, so staged content that
was never committed is not discarded.

commits.headline: fix(todoist): one rule for board writes to a task that sits in the Inbox
commits.body:
In all scope every board write now checks where the task is at its own
fresh read. In the Inbox a transition only takes off the hub's labels
and posts its comment: nothing is added, moved, dated or closed, so a
finished run whose close never landed no longer closes an Inbox task.

needs-jack is let go of as soon as it moves to the Inbox, and a comment
on a held Inbox task is not taken as an answer.

"Hybrid interaction failed: terminated" and left "[Previous voice turn failed
before a complete reply...]". The chat server needs ~20 s to listen again, but
the retry backoff is 1 s + 2 s,

flitzbaer.com's zone sends Cache-Control max-age=14400 on .js/.css,
overriding Pages' max-age=0, while HTML revalidates every time. After a
deploy, returning visitors got the new HTML with up to 4-hour-old scripts:
the account page rendered empty and the funnel broke.

commits.headline: fix(jobs): dedupe save retries and survive concurrent saves
commits.body:
- The homepage keeps the pending job id while the choices are unchanged, so
  retrying after a lost response hits the server's id dedupe instead of
  saving the job twice. A successful save clears it.
- POST /api/jobs reads the list back after writing. If a concurrent save from
  another tab replaced it, the job is merged again on the fresh list (up to
  three tries). Clerk metadata has no atomic update; this converges without
  new storage.

commits.body:
When the browser that priced a job saved it with POST /api/jobs, the copy on

it and re-applied its opt-in, reversing an opt-out made in between.

commits.headline: fix(account): load production ClerkJS and use the hosted Account Portal (#12)
commits.body:
## Why
Signing in on https://flitzbaer.com/account showed "Sign-in cannot be
reached right now". The CSP in `site/_headers` only allowed
`*.clerk.com` / `*.clerk.accounts.dev`, so the browser blocked ClerkJS
from the production Frontend API `clerk.flitzbaer.com` and the page fell
back to its error message.

commits.headline: fix: list Checkout Sessions for order history (#11)
commits.body:
Stripe has no Search API for Checkout Sessions: `GET
/v1/checkout/sessions/search` is read as a retrieve of a session named
"search" and returns 400, so `/api/account/orders` answered 502 for
every signed-in user in production (verified against live Clerk + the
test Stripe key).

commits.headline: feat: redirect alias hosts to flitzbaer.com for live Clerk sessions (#10)
commits.body:
Production Clerk (live instance on flitzbaer.com) only issues sessions
for flitzbaer.com and its subdomains. This adds a Pages middleware that
301s GET/HEAD requests on the other production hosts (www.flitzbaer.com,
flitzbear.com, the .de and .berlin domains, flitzbaer.pages.dev,
flitzbaer.autojack.ai) to https://flitzbaer.com, keeping path and query.
Preview branch aliases keep the dev Clerk keys and are not redirected.
POSTs pass through.

commits.headline: fix(agents): adopt a paused task's orphaned CLI after a worker restart
commits.body:
A worker restart (nodemon on a pull, a .env write, .hub-restart) leaves the
tmux CLI it was watching alive. Expired-lease recovery only considered tasks
still `running`, so when the CLI had already raised a question over the agent
bridge (task `awaiting_input`) or been answered (`pending`), its attempt sat
`running` with a dead lease and no worker ever read its exit.

finished, was admitted because the current turn was terminal. That regressed
the tracked turn to A and announced a duplicate terminal update with a newer
clock. A mismatched end is now accepted only when no current turn is known
(first sight), so an end closes only the turn it names.

commits.headline: fix(agents): rebuild the rollout tracker after a failed observe
commits.body:
A failed upsertStatus left the byte cursor unmoved but the per-thread
telemetry tracker had already taken that poll's tool and usage facts, so the
replay deduplicated them away and the progress update was lost for good after
one transient write failure (e.g. a WAL-lock timeout). Drop the tracker when
observing a thread fails: the next poll takes the existing restart path and
rebuilds it from the bounded tail behind the cursor, regenerating the update.

commits.headline: perf(telemetry): index agent_runs(updated_at, id) for the cursor scans
commits.body:
The owner cursor scan orders agent_runs by (updated_at, id) but no index
started with updated_at, so every poll fetched every wide row and sorted
it in a temp b-tree (29.1 ms idle at 844 rows, linear in retained runs).
A record_kind-leading index cannot serve `record_kind != ...`, so add the
plain (updated_at, id) index. The plan is still an ordered index scan, not
a constant-time lookup; it avoids the wide-row scan and the sort.

commits.headline: fix(telemetry): scope capture identity to the kernel attempt
commits.body:
Kernel attempts of one task share its session log path and
TmuxManager.createSession() truncates it, so a capture id hashed from the
path alone gave a retry the same sourceRecordId as the attempt before it
whenever both emitted a byte-identical record at the same offset (e.g. a
repeated tool call after same-length thread ids). A durable consumer
deduplicating on sourceRecordId would drop the later attempt's record.

fix(telemetry): keep superseded attempts out of current snapshots

fix(telemetry): keep usage provenance and source-time order; 400 on repeated stream filters
commits.body:
- stream(): parse filters inside the guarded block, so `?taskId=a&taskId=b` is a
  structured 400 instead of an unhandled rejection that hangs the request.
- Usage meters keep their latest cumulative snapshot plus the deltas it does not
  cover. Source time decides coverage: a late snapshot keeps newer deltas
  (T1=10, delta T3=5, late T2=15 -> 20) and a late delta after a newer snapshot
  adds nothing. Ties and untimed events follow arrival order and are labelled
  (`ordering`, `arrivalOrdered`

feat(telemetry): journal managed run live telemetry from the executor into the agent event stream
commits.body:
AgentExecutor's CLI branch taps context.onLiveTelemetry in the host process and
writes the root task's usage, context, tool and identity facts to the shared
journal through a bounded, non-blocking queue. Usage is one cumulative meter per
attempt, the producer's lowerBound/unavailable coverage is preserved and shown in
snapshot sums, queue/store failures surface as telemetry_gap diagnostics, and
child-task callbacks are never labelled with the parent's attempt.

commits.headline: feat(telemetry): /v1/agent-events ingest, replay, resumable SSE and snapshot read model
commits.body:
Slice of #2414 on top of the durable event store. Ingest, bounded replay, a
resumable SSE stream (Last-Event-ID/after, heartbeat ids, explicit reset, drain
timeout) and a snapshot folded at one fixed watermark, all on the v1 router behind
its existing gate. The projection keeps task/attempt/session/harness/provider/model
apart, fences stale producer clocks, never promotes an older attempt, and labels
partial usage and incomplete coverage instead of inferring totals.

commits.headline: fix(telemetry): make Claude replays idempotent across invocations
commits.body:
Review finding on #2416: a replayed `result` advanced the invocation counter,
so the duplicate landed in a fresh accumulator and bypassed its sourceId
dedupe (one result of 10 input / 100 output tokens and $0.50 became 220 tokens
and $1.00). Replayed assistant messages had the same hole once a result had
advanced the invocation.

commits.headline: fix(telemetry): attach the reported session to model and tool facts
commits.body:
Review finding on #2416: usage facts carried the per-event scope with the
reported session_id, but model facts and tool facts kept the constructor
scope, so a consumer could not tell which session they belonged to. Pass the
event's scope to both. With no session reported the scope is unchanged.

commits.headline: fix(telemetry): remember event identities across prune so retries cannot double-count
commits.body:
#2414 requires that replay, reconnect and retries cannot double-count. Dedupe
ran against the retained events table, so after prune an identical retry of the
same (producer, eventId) was admitted as a new event and a replayed delta usage
measurement counted twice.

commits.headline: fix(install): run @latest so npx works inside a clone (#295)
commits.body:
npm treats any spec the current folder's package already satisfies
(unpinned, a range, or the exact version) as the local project and runs
its bin from PATH. Inside a clone of this repo without a global install,
`npx -y @verygoodplugins/mcp-automem` fails with `sh: mcp-automem: not
found`; with one it silently runs the global build. A dist-tag is never
satisfied locally.

commits.headline: perf(server): trim tool parameter descriptions (#294)
commits.body:
Every tools/list byte loads into the agent's context on every turn, on both
transports. Cut the per-parameter descriptions in all six tools' input and
output schemas: drop text that repeats the top-level description, restates
an enum or default, or only gives examples. Keep the facts an agent needs to
pick a mode or avoid an error (ID fetch vs enumeration vs ranked, offset only
with exhaustive, tag_match semantics, the response budget, batch exclusions).

destination) and tells the user to enter the URL and key in Cursor ->
Customize -> Automem -> Configure. --cursor-mode files (or
AUTOMEM_CURSOR_MODE=files) keeps the mcp.json + project rule + hook install.

commits.headline: feat(cli): add `close` to shut tabs Browser Hand opened
commits.body:
`browser-hand close` closes a tab through the existing Target.closeTarget
path. It needs an explicit selector (--page-name, --query, --target-*, or
--group-title) and never falls back to the active tab. A selector that
matches several tabs is refused unless --all is passed; a lone
--group-title closes the whole Browser Hand tab group.

commits.headline: fix(agent-kernel): redact quoted credential fields in serialized errors (#2401)
commits.body:
Serialized JSON in an error message, such as
`{"password":"hunter2hunter2","token":"..."}`, slipped past the credential
assignment pattern because the closing quote after the field name broke the
`name\s*[=:]` match, so both values reached the outbox and the webhook body.

commits.headline: fix(agent-kernel): redact bare password=/token= credential assignments (#2401)
commits.body:
The credential-assignment pattern in redactSecrets required at least one
letter before the credential name, so `password=hunter2hunter2` and
`token=abcdefghijklmnop1234` passed through unchanged into the outbox and
the outbound webhook body (summary and details). Only prefixed names such
as API_KEY= were caught. Drop the prefix requirement and add a regression
test covering password=, token=, secret: and API_KEY= both directly and
through buildTaskEventPayload.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): normalize CRLF in round checkpoint narratives before hashing
commits.body:
buildCheckpointDocument hashed and stored a narrative's CRLF bytes, but
parseCheckpointDocument converts CRLF to LF before it verifies the hash. A
checkpoint the writer persisted therefore failed its own reader with a hash
mismatch, and GET /api/agent-tasks/:id swallowed that and reported no
checkpoint. Normalize in the builder, so the document that is hashed, stored
and read back is the same LF form, and cover the round trip through the writer.

The legacy unpaired pick can name capture and playback differently
(Loopback Capture / Loopback Playback). The agent was handed the input
label for its output priority and system output pattern too, so the full
smoke could not use the route its preflight had just passed. Pin input
and output separately; the shared preference matches both, as the
configured pattern did before devices were pinned.

commits.headline: fix(voice): detach the Suno poller and gate the stage pack on stage mode
commits.body:
The hub shell tool waits for `sh -c` to exit and kills the process group at
its 30 s default timeout, so the runbook's plain `node
scripts/suno-play-when-ready.mjs ...` was killed long before Suno finished
and stalled the turn 30 s. The runbook command now detaches itself with
`nohup ... &` (the form the stage shell allowlist accepts), and the pack says
the trailing `&` is what returns control.

commits.headline: fix(voice): fail the stage preflight when the stage bundle is not armed
commits.body:
VOICE_STAGE_MODE=false or 0 used to report stage-bundle ok and the run
ended GO with the bundle off. Resolve it with the agent's own
parseBooleanEnv so preflight and agent agree, and fail (not warn) when it
is not truthy. Also fail when VOICE_SHELL_ALLOW_REGEX does not compile,
since in stage mode that closes the shell entirely. Both details say the
flag must live in .env: the chat server reads the env it started with.

counted toward consecutiveTtsFailureCount. The abort reason was a plain
Error, which classifyGenerateError reads as 'error'. Abort with an
AbortError instead, so the metric is 'cancelled', the one status the TTS
failure accounting exempts.

commits.headline: fix(voice): defer an announcement preempted during its identity lookup
commits.body:
Essential speech can preempt the lane while the announcement awaits its
agent identity voice. The abort fires before the cancellation listener
is attached and is not replayed, so synthesis started anyway and the
essential speech waited behind it. Check the lane signal before starting.

commits.headline: fix(voice): close lifecycle speech that keeps losing its gap
commits.body:
The hub re-sends undelivered lifecycle speech on every 5 s outbox poll,
and the voice agent forgets an announcement once its 20 s TTL expires,
so a completion that never found a quiet gap was queued and synthesized
again at every mic open, indefinitely and across sessions. On
2026-10-26, lifecycle:agent-fp-…:185:completed (282 chars) looped from
14:08 to 14:44 UTC and was never heard.

commits.headline: fix(voice): cancel announcement synthesis once it can no longer play
commits.body:
A queued announcement (lifecycle completion, hub notice, timer) starts
synthesis the moment the session looks idle, which is often the mic-open
right before the user speaks. Qwen3-TTS serves one request per endpoint,
so the reply's first chunk waited out the whole ~6 s synthesis of audio
that was then discarded as announcement_deferred.

commits.body:
The Slack local lane had no way to read a URL. Its core tools offer only
dev_browser and open_url, and the link rule told it to use dev_browser, whose
snapshot reads whatever Chrome tab is active. Asked what a thread's blog post
said, the live model snapshotted and answered "The page wouldn't load".
URLs in the current message already route to the cloud, so this hit links
earlier in a thread.

commits.body:
Slack's thread and channel history reached both lanes with raw <@U…>
mention ids; only the current turn went through humanizeSlackMentions. In
C09CT1X5Z0S on 2026-10-22 the local model saw "Jack Arturo: <@UPB5M817W>
you inspired yesterday's blog post" and had to guess who "you" was. Run
every history message through the same humanizer, so mentions read
@Display Name (and the bot's own as @AutoJack), resolved in parallel
before the loop. A persisted turn now matches its Slack copy exactly.

Kill only the listener in kill-port.sh
commits.body:
`lsof -t -iTCP:<port>` lists every process with a socket on the port,
including clients connected to it. On 2026-10-22 a nodemon restart of the
Slack server ran `kill-port.sh 8765`, which also SIGKILLed cloudflared
through its keep-alive connections to the origin. The tunnel exited 137,
nothing restarted it, and Slack failed over to the cloud worker for 29
minutes with the hub up. Filter with -sTCP:LISTEN so only the process
holding the port is killed.

Async embedding jobs now retry bounded provider and Qdrant failures,
reuse vectors only while their source text remains current, and expose
failure/exhaustion counters in `/health.embedding`. The worker waits for

commits.headline: fix(recovery): preserve existing graph data during Qdrant salvage (#263)
commits.body:
Qdrant recovery previously deleted the graph before fetching its source
and could report success after incomplete restoration. Recovery now
validates the complete source, inserts missing memories with original
IDs and API-compatible properties, preserves existing nodes and
relationships, and fails clearly on incomplete recovery. The monitor
avoids graph salvage for a vector deficit and honors CLI > environment >
defaults, including zero.

prs.body:
## Summary
A successful npm publish can remain unavailable while npm processes the package, causing immediate MCP Registry validation to reject a real release. Wait for the exact package/version from the tagged metadata to become visible on npm before submitting it to the MCP Registry. Retry only an explicit registry rejection that this same package/version is not yet visible; stop on authorization, metadata, unexpected, or ambiguous publication failures.

prs.title: feat(tags): manage tags and preserve thread dates
prs.body:
## Summary
Add one `freescout_tags` tool for listing tags and adding, removing, or replacing a ticket's tags, plus a native tag filter on search. Add/remove read all existing tag pages and refuse to write when pagination is incomplete or inconsistent. FreeScout has no conditional update, so concurrent tag edits can still be overwritten between the read and write.

prs.title: fix(threads): accept empty creation responses
prs.body:
## Summary
FreeScout can confirm thread creation with an empty 201 response and a Resource-ID header. Accept that response for notes and drafts, retain a valid ID when supplied, and report a successful draft with `draftId: null` when it is unavailable. Parse successful responses outside the retry loop so a malformed response cannot cause a duplicate write.

prs.title: fix(tickets): omit threads when excluded
prs.body:
## Summary
FreeScout may embed threads in detail responses even when `embed=threads` is omitted. Remove them from the returned conversation when callers set `includeThreads: false`, preserving other metadata and the distinction between omitted and empty threads. The README clarifies that the upstream payload may still contain them.

## Summary
- A `git init` checkout has files and no commit, so cutting a worktree dies on `HEAD^{commit}`. Seed one root commit when the repository has no history at all, and still refuse when some other branch already has history.

prs.title: fix(speech): await final results and preserve turn ownership
prs.body: Local Speech previously committed its partial text and canceled recognition before Apple Speech could deliver corrected trailing words. Manual Send could also classify an empty partial as an empty turn before a final arrived. This change ends audio and waits up to 750 ms for the corrected final, with the latest nonempty partial as a bounded timeout/error fallback. It preserves turn ownership and a newer utterance's capture state through older transcript handoffs and server echoes.

Each persona is a gemma-4 abliterated brain with a Chatterbox voice clone (`../uncensored-voice-server/voices/<id>.wav`). The spoken aliases (`carrie`/`fisher`/`leia`, `dolly`/`parton`, `thatcher`/`margaret`/`maggie`) let you pick one by name.
